recent_posts.title: FOSS weekly roundup covering Ubuntu attacks, Linux exploit, PS5 Linux port and more
recent_posts.summary: This week's FOSS Weekly covers Ubuntu's DDoS attack that took down ubuntu.com, the Snap store, and Launchpad, followed by its Twitter account being compromised for a crypto scam. A Linux local privilege escalation exploit called 'Copy Fail' was disclosed. On the positive side, the Dutch government is building a Forgejo-based code hosting platform, Germany's Sovereign Tech Agency launched a paid program for open standards participation, and someone ported Linux to the PS5 with Steam and GTA V running. VS Code was caught crediting Copilot for commits written by humans, and Microsoft open-sourced early MS-DOS code under MIT. Other highlights include Linux Mint HWE ISOs, a Flatpak getting-started guide, Ptyxis replacing GNOME Terminal in Ubuntu 26.04, and a video guide on upgrading to Ubuntu 26.04.

recent_posts.title: Getting started with Yazi terminal file manager on Linux
recent_posts.summary: Yazi is a feature-rich, Rust-based terminal file manager that offers image and file previews, syntax highlighting, fuzzy search via fzf, ripgrep-powered content search, bulk rename, multi-tab interface, and zoxide integration. A wrapper shell function lets you cd into the last browsed directory on exit. Installation is covered for Arch Linux, Ubuntu (Snap), and generic binary installs, along with optional dependencies like ffmpeg, fd, and ripgrep that unlock its full capabilities.

recent_posts.title: After Days of DDoS, Now Ubuntu's Twitter Account Seems to be Compromised
recent_posts.summary: Ubuntu's official Twitter account was compromised and used to promote a fake AI agent called 'Numbat', leveraging Ubuntu's real branding, Solana blockchain references, and a near-identical domain (ai-ubuntu.com) to lure users into a crypto wallet scam. The attack followed a five-day DDoS assault on Canonical's web infrastructure starting April 30, which took down ubuntu.com, the Snap store, and Launchpad. A pro-Iran hacker group called 313 claimed responsibility for the DDoS but has not been linked to the Twitter compromise. The two incidents may or may not be connected, and Canonical has yet to release a post-incident report.

recent_posts.title: Open source PCB replacement gives Google Home Mini local voice processing for $85
recent_posts.summary: MiciMike ReV Devices has created an $85 drop-in PCB replacement for the original Google Home Mini (1st gen), giving the discontinued smart speaker a second life with local voice processing. The board uses an ESP32-S3 as the main processor and an XMOS XU316 for audio processing, with two MEMS microphones, wake word detection via microWakeWord, and ESPHome preinstalled for integration with Home Assistant. All voice data stays on-device, the original speaker is reused, and the hardware mute button physically disconnects the microphones. The design files are open source under CERN-OHL-S v2 and available on GitHub. Available on Crowd Supply for $85, shipping estimated October 2026, with a Nest Mini version also planned.

recent_posts.title: LibreOffice Questions Whether Euro-Office is Truly Sovereign
recent_posts.summary: The Document Foundation (TDF), the nonprofit behind LibreOffice, is publicly questioning whether Euro-Office — a new European office suite forked from ONLYOFFICE by Nextcloud and IONOS — is truly sovereign. TDF's concern centers on document format: Euro-Office's launch materials emphasize Microsoft Office (OOXML) compatibility rather than committing to ODF (Open Document Format) as its native default. TDF argues that real digital sovereignty requires open formats like ODF, an ISO standard not controlled by any single company, rather than just self-hosting software that remains structurally tied to Microsoft's format decisions. Euro-Office has not responded to TDF's public inquiry, and the question carries legal weight given Germany's existing ODF mandate.

recent_posts.title: Copy Fail Linux kernel privilege escalation vulnerability explained
recent_posts.summary: A 9-year-old logic flaw in the Linux kernel (CVE-2026-31431, dubbed 'Copy Fail') allows any unprivileged local user to escalate to root using a 732-byte Python script. The bug lives in the kernel's cryptographic subsystem and corrupts 4 bytes of a file's in-memory copy without touching the on-disk file, bypassing integrity checks. It was patched in mainline on April 1 after responsible disclosure. Risk is highest for multi-tenant hosts, Kubernetes clusters, CI runners, and cloud environments where the page cache is shared across container boundaries. Desktop users with updated kernels face low risk. CISA has added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and ordered US federal agencies to patch by May 15. A temporary mitigation is blacklisting the algif_aead kernel module.

recent_posts.title: Netherlands launches self-hosted Forgejo platform for government source code
recent_posts.summary: The Netherlands is building a sovereign, self-hosted Git platform for government source code using Forgejo, a fully open source forge licensed under GPLv3+. GitHub was ruled out for being proprietary, and GitLab for its open-core model. The platform, code.overheid.nl, soft-launched on April 24, 2026, and is already hosting repositories from the Dutch Electoral Council, the Ministry of the Interior, and several municipalities. Still in pilot phase, it aims to reduce duplicate development across agencies and give the government full control over its infrastructure.

recent_posts.title: VS Code was silently adding Copilot as a git co-author on all commits
recent_posts.summary: VS Code quietly began adding a 'Co-authored-by: Copilot' trailer to git commits after a pull request in April changed the default value of the git.addAICoAuthor setting from 'off' to 'all'. This meant any user who hadn't manually configured the setting had Copilot credited in their git history — even on commits written entirely without AI assistance. The trailer also appeared when Copilot features were explicitly disabled, and was appended after commit finalization with no chance to review it. A VS Code team member acknowledged the mistake on Hacker News, apologized, and a fix reverting the default back to 'off' has been merged and is expected in VS Code 1.119.

recent_posts.title: A Free Open Source Mobile Dev Hackathon Is Coming to the Netherlands on May 16
recent_posts.summary: OS-SCi, a Netherlands-based FOSS education institution, is hosting the Lomiri Tech Meeting — a free two-day hackathon on May 16–17, 2026 in Tilburg. The event targets students interested in open source mobile development for Lomiri and Ubuntu Touch. Attendees will hear keynotes from Lomiri UI project leader Mike Gabriel and Erik Mols, who will announce a new Lomiri Bounty Program offering real-world incentives for contributing to the Ubuntu Touch ecosystem. All participants receive free copies of Lomiri App Development Level 1 and Level 2 books. The event includes hands-on app development sessions guided by experts and is open to students of all experience levels.

recent_posts.title: What Are Linux Mint HWE ISOs and Do You Actually Need One?
recent_posts.summary: Linux Mint has released HWE (Hardware Enablement) ISO images for Linux Mint 22.3, shipping with Linux kernel 6.17 instead of the standard 6.14. These are not new releases but alternative installation images designed for users with very new hardware that may not be supported by the older kernel. Existing Mint 22.3 users who are already up to date likely already have kernel 6.17 and don't need these ISOs. The HWE ISOs are primarily useful at install time for machines where the regular ISO fails to boot or install. Users with NVIDIA, Broadcom, or VirtualBox setups should be cautious, as proprietary modules can have compatibility issues on newer kernels. The Mint team plans to continue releasing updated HWE ISOs as newer kernels land, bridging the gap until Linux Mint 23 arrives in December 2026.

top_posts.title: 19 popular VS Code themes for better visual coding experience
top_posts.summary: A curated collection of 19 popular VS Code themes ranging from dark options like Dracula and One Dark Pro to light alternatives like GitHub Theme and Bluloco Light. Each theme is presented with key features, highlighting aspects like readability, contrast, color palettes, and suitability for different coding environments and preferences.

top_posts.title: Firefox 149 ships Brave's adblock-rust engine disabled by default
top_posts.summary: Firefox 149 quietly shipped adblock-rust, Brave's open-source Rust-based ad and tracker blocking engine, without mentioning it in the release notes. The integration was filed as a Bugzilla bug titled 'Add a prototype rich content blocking engine' and is currently disabled by default with no UI or filter lists. The engine supports uBlock Origin-compatible filter list syntax and handles network request blocking and cosmetic filtering. Waterfox, a Firefox fork, has also adopted the same implementation. A step-by-step guide is provided to enable and test the feature via about:config using EasyList and EasyPrivacy filter lists.

top_posts.title: Danish road traffic authority pilots open source migration from Microsoft
top_posts.summary: Denmark's Road Traffic Authority is piloting SIA Open, a government initiative to replace Microsoft Windows and Office applications with open source alternatives. The agency cites data sovereignty and avoiding vendor lock-in as key motivations. This pilot involves a portion of their 600 employees, with plans to expand to 15,000 government users across multiple state agencies. The specific open source alternatives haven't been disclosed yet.

top_posts.title: Go language co-creator Rob Pike criticizes AI-generated appreciation email
top_posts.summary: Rob Pike, co-creator of the Go programming language and legendary computer scientist from Bell Labs, expressed outrage after receiving an AI-generated thank-you email. The email came from an AI agent participating in the AI Village project, where agents were tasked with performing "random acts of kindness" and interpreted this by sending unsolicited emails to famous programmers. Pike's angry response highlights concerns about AI-generated content wasting resources, the environmental cost of AI infrastructure, and the broader societal impact of meaningless AI-generated material flooding our digital spaces.

top_posts.title: Systemd’s New Feature Brings Age Verification Option to Linux
top_posts.summary: Systemd has merged a pull request adding an optional `birthDate` field to its userdb JSON user records, responding to age verification laws in California, Colorado, and Brazil. The field, stored in YYYY-MM-DD format, can only be set by administrators and is not mandatory. Lennart Poettering clarified that systemd itself does nothing with the data — it simply standardizes the field so other projects like xdg-desktop-portal can build age verification compliance on top of it. A request to repeal the change was rejected, with Poettering noting widespread misunderstanding of the intent.
